 OPB’s First Look: Cyrus Javadi faces voters after party switch
 By Winston Szeto ( OPB ) Oct. 24, 2026 4:39 p.m. Subscribe to OPB’s First Look to receive Northwest news in your inbox six days a week. 
 THANKS TO OUR SPONSOR: Become a Sponsor Good morning, Northwest.
 Oregon state Rep. Cyrus Javadi has twice won election to represent House District 32 on the North Coast — both times as a Republican. Now, after switching parties last year, he’s seeking reelection as a Democrat. With Election Day less than two weeks away, can he win a third term under a different party banner? OPB’s Dirk VanderHart spoke with Javadi and his Republican challenger, Max Sherman .
 Here’s your First Look at Saturday’s news.
 — Winston Szeto
 Top stories
 Oregon state Rep. Cyrus Javadi, D-Tillamook, waves to a vehicle passing by while canvassing on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026, in Tillamook, Ore.
 Jenny Kane for OPB / OPB 
 Cyrus Javadi switched parties. Will his Oregon district reelect him anyway?
 Republican lawmaker Cyrus Javadi shocked his party last year when he voted for a package of transportation tax and fee hikes introduced by Gov. Tina Kotek that included an unpopular 6-cent gas tax increase.
 Then, perhaps recognizing Republicans would never reward such apostasy with reelection, he switched parties.
 Now Javadi’s up for reelection.
 He has won his coastal district — stretching from Astoria down to Neskowin — twice. But he did so as a Republican. On Nov. 3, he’ll find out how voters feel about his political moves. (Dirk VanderHart)

 FILE - Ballots move through a signature verification system at the Multnomah County Elections Division office in Portland, Ore., Nov. 1, 2024. 
 Kristyna Wentz-Graff / OPB 
 Federal election monitors will be on hand in Portland on Election Day
 The Trump administration is sending monitors to watch vote counting in Oregon’s most liberal county on Election Day.
 In an email Thursday, the U.S. Department of Justice told state elections officials it will send an unspecified number of election monitors from its Civil Rights Division to Multnomah County on Nov. 3 as staff accept and process ballots.
 THANKS TO OUR SPONSOR: Become a Sponsor The DOJ told Bloomberg earlier this year it would deploy up to 1,000 such monitors nationwide — even as the administration bucks decades of precedent by not allowing international election observers to scrutinize the midterms. (Dirk VanderHart)

 3 things to know
 FILE - The sun sets over the U.S. Coast Guard facility at the Newport Municipal Airport, where the rescue helicopter typically is and near the area that Immigration and Customs Enforcement is seemingly considering for a facility in Newport, Ore., on Nov. 17, 2025.
 Eli Imadali / OPB 
 Yesterday, the Department of Homeland Security, which oversees the Immigration and Customs Enforcement, confirmed in federal court filings that it has abandoned plans to build a detention center in Newport and that it presently has no plans to build anywhere in Oregon. (Courtney Sherwood) 
 Yesterday, the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality notified Precision Castparts Corp. that it had committed “the most serious violations” of Oregon environmental law, causing an industrial chemical leak that killed multiple fish in Portland’s Johnson Creek in late September. (April Ehrlich) 
 Students at Oregon State University’s Cascades campus in Bend are worried about their safety after alleged incidents of sexual assault that took place on early October and the Silver Rail Elementary School shooting. (Natalie Pate)

 One more look
 Call this caramel apple compote King Midas because everything it touches turns to gold
 Heather Arndt Anderson / OPB 
 Superabundant recipe: This warm caramel apple compote turns everything it touches to gold
 The apple may not have fallen far from the tree, but it’s certainly spread across the globe for centuries.
 So have recipes for apple desserts.
 There’s a recipe for stewed apples in ancient Mesopotamian tablets, and spiced fruit preserves called murabba appeared in the 10th century.
 Today’s recipe puts its own twist on using the fruit as a sweet treat. It’s saucy, rich and buttery like a proper caramel sauce should be, and the apples stay tender and crisp, cooked just enough to soften on the edges. ( Heather Arndt Anderson)
